To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“A Semantic Web based approach to representing the intent of a scientific workflow can facilitate the monitoring of workflow execution and the interpretation of experimental results.”
a Semantic Web approach to workflow can be beneficial in terms of workflow provenance and monitoring, and in providing an abstract model of scientific intent.
the use of semantic descriptions of scientist’s intent in workflow experiments can enhance the design, execution and interpretation of workflow studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of semantics in workflow systems to enhance the design, execution and analysis of workflow experiments and studies.
the development and evaluation of an abstract model of scientific intent and a framework for its realisation using Semantic Web technologies.
the design and use of workflow tools which support the scientific process by providing the scientist with the ability to describe the intent of their workflow experiment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research has demonstrated the feasibility of using Semantic Web technologies to enhance the workflow process in terms of the design, execution and interpretation of workflow models.
the framework proposed in this paper provides the means for a more effective workflow design, execution, monitoring, provenance and annotation.
the use of semantics in the design of workflows can enhance the way in which scientists design, execute, analyse and interpret their experiments and studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that it is feasible to use semantic technologies to enhance workflow systems and to provide scientists with the ability to describe the intent behind their experiments and to monitor the results in a way that facilitates the interpretation of the results.
the proposed approach can be used to enhance the design, execution and analysis of scientific workflows.
the use of semantic technologies to represent scientific intent is beneficial in enhancing the workflow experience for the scientists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by incorporating semantics into a workflow system, the system can better assist the user to understand the provenance of data and the results of the workflow experiment.
the use of semantics in workflow tools has the potential to enhance the way that scientists work and to provide a richer description of their experimental results and their provenance.
the use of a semantic representation of intent can facilitate the analysis of workflow experiments, which can in turn enhance the reproducibility of scientific studies.
